ZEUS: King of Olympus, and he throws the lightning
HERA: Queen of the Greek gods, and a very jealous wife
ARES: Greek god of war, and the Roman Mars
EROS: Greek god of desire, with a bow and arrow
THOR: The god of thunder, and his hammer
ODIN: One-eyed all-father of the Norse gods
LOKI: Norse trickster who fathered a wolf and a serpent
FREYA: Norse goddess of love, in a cat-drawn chariot
BALDR: Norse god of light, killed by a sprig of mistletoe
APOLLO: Greek god of the sun, music and prophecy
ATHENA: Greek goddess of wisdom, born from Zeus's head
ARTEMIS: Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon
HERMES: Winged messenger of the Greek gods
HESTIA: Greek goddess of the hearth and home
DEMETER: Greek goddess of the harvest, mother of Persephone
POSEIDON: Greek god of the sea, with a trident
CRONUS: Titan who ate his children, father of Zeus
TITAN: The elder race the Olympians overthrew
MEDUSA: Snakes for hair, and one look turns you to stone
HYDRA: Cut off one head and two grow back
SPHINX: Asks a riddle, and eats you if you fail
MINOTAUR: Bull-headed man at the centre of the labyrinth
OSIRIS: Egyptian god of the afterlife, killed by his brother
ANUBIS: Jackal-headed Egyptian god who weighs the heart
HORUS: Falcon-headed Egyptian god, and that famous eye
RAGNAROK: The Norse end of the world
VALHALLA: Odin's hall where slain warriors feast
OLYMPUS: The mountain where the Greek gods lived
ICARUS: Flew too close to the sun on wax wings
